title: Should You Buy Alibaba Stock Before the Huge Investor Update? | BABA Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc asks whether Alibaba is a buying opportunity on the dip before its 19 November earnings update, running his updated discounted cash flow model against the stock's slide from above $175 early in 2026 to $94, its lowest point of the year and down 36%. He notes the paradox that the share price is falling while Wall Street earnings estimates rise: EPS is expected to grow about 27% a year, but much of that growth is funded by heavy capital expenditure on AI infrastructure and proprietary chips rather than organic growth, which he illustrates with a restaurant-owner analogy. Margins have also declined for most of the past decade, with operating margin down from about 30% to low single digits and cash flow from operations to sales from over 50% to single digits. The balance sheet is strong, with over $63 billion in cash and short-term investments against under $35 billion of long-term debt, so the AI buildout can be funded without new borrowing. Valuation is the attraction: forward P/E of just 10, down from 25 earlier in 2026, with AI revenue growing at triple-digit percentages. Call: BABA BUY at ~$94, DCF fair value $122, first tracked; buy before earnings for higher risk/reward or wait until after the print. Bull: AI acceleration and proprietary chips cut AI costs, and a re-rate from a P/E of 10. Bear: margins in long decline and earnings growth is capex-funded, not organic. (Auto-captions garble the sponsor name as 'mly full' for The Motley Fool.)

Buy before earnings for higher risk/reward, or wait until after the print for lower risk - either way a buy.

calls.bull_case: AI revenue acceleration plus proprietary chips lower AI costs; valuation re-rates from fwd P/E 10 toward earlier 25.
